violation_type.title: Renewal background checks submitted - When change in role requires subject to have fingerprint-based check now instead of only name-based TX check (26 TAC §745.621(b)(3))
violation_type.short_title: Renewal background checks submitted - When change in role requires subject to have fingerprint-based check now instead of only name-based TX check
violation_type.typical_finding: Based on the DFPS investigation, a staff member's role changed from volunteer to caregiver when left alone with a child on multiple occasions.

finding_variants.text: Based on the DFPS investigation, a staff member's role changed from volunteer to caregiver when left alone with a child on multiple occasions.
Three volunteers did not have the required background check submitted. One volunteer was serving in the role of a caregiver counted in ratio. The caregiver role requires fingerprints to be submitted.

A caregiver who routinely works for the operation 5 days a week and counted in ratio did not have the required fingerprint check when their background checks were renewed.    The caregiver was not present during the inspection but has been employed since 2016 and had a previous fingerprint check.
A caregiver's role was not correctly changed from volunteer to caregiver at the time of renewal so that a fingerprint-based check could be conducted as required.

The provider, the household member, and the assistant caregiver have an inactive background check on file.  The background checks were previously submitted less than 5 years from the dates from when the background checks  were initially submitted.
The role of a volunteer changed to an employee role two months ago. Operation has not submitted a renewal background check with the employee's current role.
